method: Read-only review of runtime diffs, new modules, repair/persistence paths and test evidence, following review-agent instructions. Performed by the implementation agent, not an independent reviewer. Implementation fixes were made outside the review.
resolvedFindings: Keep broken-rod angle memory separate from oscillating wheel play to prevent accumulating wobble into steering.
Refuse bleeding an empty circuit; refill retains trapped air and enables its separate service action.
A wheel seized by its bearing also feeds actual locked sliding work into tyre flat spots.
Anchor both broken tie-rod halves to the remaining rack/wheel endpoints.
limits: Bounded fictional bearing, steering and diagonal brake models. Shared pad/disc health; no multibody suspension, pipe CFD, vacuum reservoir or real-car calibration. Bearing heat uses final angular speed times friction impulse.
Pedal travel is normalized diagnostic telemetry; cockpit/pedal animation remains open. Detailed component state is not transmitted to remote car models.
Final-HTML persistence/new-run/diagnostics tested; damaged-part service additionally uses original VehiclePanel/CarPhysics in a module harness, without main service timing or driving to a garage.
Real public PeerJS/WebRTC between local processes/contexts. Separate physical PCs, mobile networks, restrictive NAT and TURN fallback not tested.
No physical controller or subjective listening test. CPU sample excludes world/GPU/AI/audio and is not an FPS guarantee.
visualCheck: Desktop and 390-pixel service panels inspected: component descriptions, damage levels and actions remain readable.
Final garage/driving screenshots inspected; existing cartoon assets retained.
